title: Design System: 東京近郊即時影像 · 車站告示系統

led-off.note: JS constant OFF in the LED renderer, not a CSS custom property.

amber.note: Also JS constants AMB/GRN/RED; LIFT/SHADE tables are keyed by this hex.

green.note: Also JS constants AMB/GRN/RED; LIFT/SHADE tables are keyed by this hex.

red.note: Also JS constants AMB/GRN/RED; LIFT/SHADE tables are keyed by this hex.

ticket.note: trip.html only. Ground of a ticket; carries a 12px diagonal hairline 地紋 hatch (#78a58a at .18).

ticket-rule.note: trip.html only. Ticket border and the 2px dashed perforation after the time column.

slab.note: trip.html only. Island platform surface on the 構內圖.

tactile.note: trip.html only. Tactile edge strip; the 9×8 SVG tile also carries a #c79a00 dot. Unchanged in dark mode.

rail.note: trip.html only. Rails and sleepers between island platforms, drawn at .7 opacity.

stop-solid.note: trip.html only. Solid red for fills and outlines: today outline and tabs, must-board border and head, the today key. White text on it at 5.8:1. Unchanged in dark mode.

station-name.purpose: Kanji on a 駅名標; kana 12px .2em above, romaji below.

line-head.purpose: Region name over its 6px line-colour rule.

title.purpose: Page title in the top bar, with a Hind romaji subtitle.

poster-head.purpose: White heading in a navy 案内 head; Japanese sign term 11px .12em beside it.

caption.purpose: Camera place name on its sign strip (13.5px below 700px).

small.purpose: Hints, sources, secondary lines in plate-2.

figure.purpose: Temperatures and readings, tabular Hind (20px on the sign, 15px road readings).

led.purpose: GNU Unifont 8×16 / 16×16 bitmaps from the LEDG table, drawn on canvas; rebuild with tools/led-glyphs.py. Not a CSS font. On trip.html: tools/led-glyphs.py --page trip.html; the countdown digit is drawn at scale 2 (every dot doubled).

eki-day.purpose: trip.html: the kanji on a day's 駅名標 (32px, .14em), kana .22em above, Hind romaji below.

facility-head.purpose: trip.html: chapter and map headings on a charcoal facility sign, Hind English term beside it.

ticket-time.purpose: trip.html: the time column of a ticket, red for booked / due / opens; a word time is 16px Eki TC.

trip-faces.purpose: Offline subsets: 'Eki TC' = Noto Sans TC 400/700 (all characters) + 900 (heading and station-name characters only), 'Eki JP' = Noto Sans JP 400/700 for Japanese-only kanji forms, 'Eki Latin' = Hind 600/700. Rebuild with python3 tools/trip-font.py after any text edit.

shadows.name: lamp-rim
shadows.purpose: Rim of a Fuji status lamp; the only box-shadow in the system.

shadows.name: bracket
shadows.value: ::before 4×14px post + ::after 38×4px bar in housing-2 above each monitor (14px top padding)
shadows.purpose: Hangs each ITV monitor; depth by mounting, not shadow.

motion.name: led-pitch
motion.value: --led-pitch 1.3 CSS px per dot (2 at ≥1100px); dp = round(pitch × devicePixelRatio)

motion.name: led-dot-rules
motion.value: dp ≥ 3: lit dot dp − max(1, floor(dp/4)) with gap; dp 2: shade cell + one bright pixel; dp 1: solid; unlit #24221f square of dp − 1 under every cell
motion.purpose: Keep the dot grid visible and the LED bright at every density.

motion.name: led-scroll
motion.value: one rAF clock, 1 dot-column per 42ms (24/s), whole-dot steps, 40-column loop gap; paused on hover/touch, off-screen and hidden tab
motion.purpose: Long route steps and the weather ticker.

motion.name: board-wipe
motion.value: 7 columns per 16ms from the left, each row delayed 24ms × row index
motion.purpose: Day change redraws the board column by column.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: no scrolling (rows wrap with CJK line-break rules), no wipe, weather defaults to the table, smooth scroll off

motion.name: signs-static
motion.value: no CSS transitions or animations anywhere
motion.purpose: Signs, panels and monitors never animate.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.value: .2s cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.3,1.3) from rotate(+6deg) scale(1.18); off under reduced motion
motion.purpose: trip.html 駅スタンプ: the one non-LED motion in the system.

motion.name: plan-board-static
motion.value: eight day rows wrap and never scroll; only the hero route row scrolls
motion.purpose: trip.html 發車時刻表: eight moving rows read as noise.

breakpoints.name: trip-fac-count
breakpoints.value: max-width: 419px (facility count drops into the tile flow)

breakpoints.name: trip-tickets-two
breakpoints.value: min-width: 900px (tickets and dishes in two columns)

breakpoints.name: trip-desktop
breakpoints.value: min-width: 1100px (board left, sticky map right; day body two columns; stay / transport boards two columns)

darkMode.note: trip.html shares tk_theme with livecam.html; fac, ticket*, slab, rail and caution* take dark values; the stamp ink turns #ff6a5c without multiply.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Station Concourse"**

The page is a Japanese railway station. You walk in through a yellow 出口 sign and reach a black LED departure board (発車標) that shows the day's itinerary in dot-matrix light. Beside it are the station's 運行情報 displays: navy-headed enamel panels that carry the weather, the Fuji lamps, the speed-limit notice and the current picks. Further down the concourse every camera area gets a white 駅名標 standing on its own line. Each sign has a line-colour band, a ringed station-number badge, the name in kana, kanji and romaji, and the previous and next stations. The area's cameras hang below the sign from brackets, like platform ITV monitors.

Everything is signage. Surfaces are flat enamel, painted housing or lit LED. Depth comes from objects hanging and standing (a bracket, a housing, a sign edge), never from soft shadows. Only the LED board moves, and it moves in LED grammar: whole-dot steps, column-by-column wipes, hard on and off. The signs never animate.

Confirmed rejection, from the direction contract: the category default of a dark CCTV wall made of same-size thumbnail cards under a hero. In this world the monitors belong to the station signs; they never form a free-standing grid of cards.

The trip itinerary (`trip.html`, station edition) is the same station read from its concourse map (構內圖). Eight days are 1–8番線 on four island platforms with rails, yellow 点字ブロック edges and a grey slab; lodging, transport, food and the checklist are facilities (飯店口, みどりの窓口, 美食街, 改札口) under charcoal facility signs. Each day is a platform under its own 駅名標. Hard commitments are pale green マルス tickets with round red station-stamp seals, and the rest of the plan sits on navy 案内 boards. The LED board carries the trip, the dates and the countdown; pressing the 駅スタンプ is the one non-LED motion.
keyCharacteristics: A station's three kinds of signage: an LED board for time-bound plans, navy-headed enamel panels for status, white 駅名標 for places.
LED text is real dot matrix: GNU Unifont 16-dot bitmaps drawn dot by dot on canvas, with the unlit dots visible.
Four line colours (TK / YS / HF / IZ) are the page's own grouping and the only chromatic accents on the signs.
Filled JIS-style pictograms from one inline SVG sprite; no outline icon sets, no emoji.
Night platform in dark mode: the concourse and panels go dark, the 駅名標 and exit sign stay lit.
On trip.html the station adds charcoal facility signs, pale green マルス tickets, island platforms with yellow tactile edges, and red ink that only marks a promise.

rules.name: The Signs Stay Lit Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is a station at night. `ground`, `plate` and the status inks change, and `navy` lifts to `#2a3a5c`. The 駅名標 (`sign`, which dims only to `#ecebe6`), the exit sign, the badges, the number plates and the LED housing keep their colours. A dark-mode screen still shows white station signs.

rules.name: The Three LEDs Rule
rules.body: An LED shows amber, green or red and nothing else. Green names (titles, times, cities), amber informs (steps, readings), red warns (notes, deadlines, a wet rain chance). The JS constants `AMB / GRN / RED` and the `LIFT` / `SHADE` tables are keyed by these exact hex values, so a new LED colour needs all three tables updated, not just the CSS token.

rules.name: The Line Is the Accent Rule
rules.body: Line colours appear only as signage geometry: bands, rules, rings and the route track. They never fill a panel or set body text. On trip.html the same holds: the 駅名標 band, the ringed 番線 badges on map, tabs and day headers, the chip ring and the 8px band on a hotel entry. Rails and slabs are neutral steel and concrete.

rules.name: The Red Is a Promise Rule
rules.body: On trip.html red (`stop` text, `stop-solid` fills, LED red) marks a hard commitment only: a booked / due / opens ticket time, a round station-stamp seal, a must board (red border, red head, 注意), today (outline, 今天 tab, today key, today board row) and the stamped 到著章. Everything else prints in ink, navy or charcoal.

rules.name: The Bilingual Sign Rule
rules.body: Place names are written the way a station writes them: kana over kanji over romaji on the 駅名標, a romaji line under the next- and previous-station names, and the Japanese sign term set after a poster head. The second language always sits **beside or below** its name in the same object. It never floats above a heading as a label of its own.

rules.name: The Lit Text Is Bitmap Rule
rules.body: Anything shown on the LED board, the board clocks or the weather ticker is drawn from Unifont bitmaps on canvas, with a screen-reader copy in a `.sr` span next to it. After changing any text the board can show, run `tools/led-glyphs.py`. A character missing from the table is rasterised from the browser font at 16px as a fallback, so it still renders, only less crisply. trip.html carries its own table: run `python3 tools/led-glyphs.py --page trip.html`.

rules.name: The LED Is for Boards Rule
rules.body: Lit dot matrix appears only on departure boards, the board clocks and the countdown digit (drawn at scale 2). Headings, tickets, tabs and chapter text are never LED. Small status tags printed on black (the facility count, the 今天 tab under the sign) are CSS text like the monitors' LIVE label, not lit dots.

rules.name: The Hung, Not Lifted Rule
rules.body: If an object needs to read as separate from the concourse, mount it: a bracket, a housing edge or a sign rule. Don't use blur shadows, glow or hover lifts. Hover changes are underline, border colour or a flat background swap. On trip.html objects stand instead: platform rows sit on a slab between rails, tickets lie flat with a perforation, chapters stand under a facility sign.

rules.name: The One Container Level Rule
rules.body: Inside a facility board (a navy-headed `group` in みどりの窓口 or 美食街) nothing draws a second box. An inner 案内 board drops its border and head fill and becomes a bold 14.5px sub-head over a 2px navy rule (red rule and `stop` text for a must board). Hotel entries are the single container of 飯店口, each banded 8px in its line colour.

dos: Do put time-bound plans on the LED board, status on navy-headed 案内 panels, and places on white 駅名標. Each kind of information has its own kind of signage.
Do draw every lit character from the Unifont table on canvas with its unlit dots, keep a `.sr` text copy beside it, and re-run `tools/led-glyphs.py` after changing board text.
Do keep LED colours to amber, green and red with their meanings (green names, amber informs, red warns), and update `AMB/GRN/RED`, `LIFT` and `SHADE` together.
Do move LEDs only in whole-dot steps or column wipes, pause scrolling on hover, touch and off-screen, and wrap instead of scrolling under reduced motion.
Do carry a region's line colour through `--line` on its bands, rules, rings and route track, and give every new area a badge code on its line (TK05, YS03…).
Do hang every camera from its bracket with a hood number plate (`LINE` + number + `-` + index) and a separate caption sign strip.
Do keep the 駅名標, exit sign, badges and housings lit in dark mode; only the concourse, panels and status inks change.
Do use the filled pictogram sprite for every icon, at 1em in `currentColor`.
Do put every hard commitment on trip.html on a マルス ticket (time behind the perforation, seal at the right) and update the ticket and the prose that mention it together.
Do head trip.html's chapters with a charcoal facility sign (white pictogram tile, 900 heading, Hind term beside) and keep one container level inside.
Do keep red for promises: booked / due / opens times, seals, must boards and today.
Do rebuild trip.html's inlined faces with `python3 tools/trip-font.py` and its LED table with `python3 tools/led-glyphs.py --page trip.html` after any text edit.
Do draw tactile edges, rails and sleepers as hard-stop patterns (SVG tile, repeating stripes); they are drawn objects, not shading.
donts: Don't lay the cameras out as a free-standing wall of same-size thumbnail cards under a hero; monitors always hang under their station sign.
Don't animate signs, panels or monitors: no fades, slides, hover lifts or easing. Motion belongs to the LED board alone (trip.html's 駅スタンプ press, 0.2s, is the single exception).
Don't add blur shadows, glow or gradients; separation is a bracket, a housing edge or a 1px rule (hard-stop pattern tiles that draw rails, sleepers and ruled memo lines are drawings, not gradients).
Don't set LED text in a CSS web font or invent a fourth LED colour.
Don't fill panels or set body text in line colours, or present TK / YS / HF / IZ as real railway lines.
Don't float the second-language term above a heading as a label; it sits beside or below its name.
Don't use emoji or outline icon sets.
Don't nest a bordered box inside a facility board, or a card inside a ticket.
Don't use red or `stop-solid` for emphasis, hover or decoration on trip.html; it means a commitment.
Don't fill a trip.html platform, ticket or board with a line colour; line colours ring badges and band signs.
